_README: Copy this file to brand-truth.json and replace every value with YOUR company's real, verifiable facts. This object is the single source of truth the whole engine writes from — every blog is grounded strictly in what's here. Garbage in = generic/hallucinated blogs out. Be specific and truthful; leave a field as an empty string/array rather than inventing.
one_liner: One sentence: what the product is + who it's for. e.g. 'Acme is AI-powered invoice reconciliation for mid-market finance teams.'
what_it_is: 2-4 plain sentences describing what you do, how it works, and the concrete outcome for the customer. No marketing fluff — a smart friend explaining it.
icp: Who genuinely buys/uses this — role, company size, industry, the situation they're in. e.g. 'Finance managers and controllers at $10M-$200M B2B companies drowning in manual AP work.'
key_facts: 5-10 concrete, VERIFIABLE facts (real features, integrations, pricing tier, markets served, certifications, real numbers).
e.g. 'Integrates natively with QuickBooks, Xero, and NetSuite.'
e.g. 'Processes invoices in under 30 seconds with 99.2% line-item accuracy.'
Each a short factual statement. NEVER invent a stat you can't back up.
differentiators: Why choose you over the alternatives — the specific wedge.
e.g. 'Unlike generic OCR tools, we reconcile against your GL automatically, not just extract text.'
features_or_ingredients: Your real features (SaaS) / ingredients or materials (D2C) / service offerings.
Copy from your actual product. Empty if not applicable.
positioning: The category you're in + your wedge, one short paragraph. e.g. 'In the AP-automation category, we're the option for teams that want reconciliation, not just data capture — built for finance, not IT.'

faqs.q: A real question your buyers ask.
faqs.a: A grounded, honest answer (feeds FAQ schema for AI citation).

faqs.q: e.g. Does it work with our existing ERP?
faqs.a: e.g. Yes — native integrations with QuickBooks, Xero, and NetSuite; others via API.

off_limits: Topics/claims you must NEVER make — legal or brand-unsafe.
e.g. medical cure claims, competitor bashing, specific financial/legal advice, guarantees you can't back.
